先聽第二小提琴與中提琴。大部分人只聽第一小提琴的旋律，但四重奏的品質往往在內聲部: Start with the second violin and the viola. Most people listen only to the melody in the first violin, but a quartet's quality usually lies in the inner parts: whether the harmony is filled in cleanly, whether the melody is propped up from below.
另一個關鍵是「聽誰」。四重奏的平衡不是四個人都聽自己，而是每個人都聽一個特定的對: Another key question is who you listen to. A quartet's balance does not come from all four listening to themselves; each player listens to one specific thing. The first violin listens to the cello's bass, the second violin listens to the first violin's intonation, the viola listens to the harmony of the two violins, and the cello listens to the viola's inner line. This order of listening can be trained, and it changes the stability of the ensemble directly. If all four listen only to themselves the sound comes apart; if all four listen to the first violin the bass disappears; when each listens to something different, the whole harmony locks together.
和弦的三音、高低音之間的空隙；音色比小提琴暗，負責厚度: The third of the chord and the space between the upper and lower voices; darker in timbre than the violin, it carries the thickness
和木管四重奏、銅管五重奏相比，差別在音色的同源與否。弦樂四重奏的四件樂器音色接近: Compared with a woodwind quartet or a brass quintet, the difference is whether the timbres come from the same source. In a string quartet the four instruments sound alike, so blending is the default and the difficulty is balance between the parts; in a wind chamber group the timbres differ, so blending is itself the problem to be solved.
和聲填充、與第一小提琴形成三度或六度；常接手旋律或與中提琴交換: Fills in the harmony, sitting a third or a sixth below the first violin; often takes over the melody or trades with the viola
四這個數字是功能算出來的。兩把小提琴分擔外聲部與內聲部的高音，中提琴填中間，大提: The number four is worked out from function. The two violins share the outer part and the upper inner part, the viola fills the middle and the cello takes the bass; four parts cover exactly the soprano, alto, tenor and bass ranges of choral writing. With three players a layer is missing; with five (adding a double bass or a second viola, say) one layer becomes heavy and the balance breaks. Four players, one voice per layer, and nobody can hide behind anyone else.
四重奏一定要四個很熟的朋友才組得成。: A quartet can only be formed by four close friends.
四重奏最特別的地方是沒有指揮。四個人坐在彼此幾步之內，每個人都聽得見另外三個人，: The most unusual thing about a quartet is that there is no conductor. The four sit a few steps from one another and each hears the other three, so tempo is not handed down but negotiated.
四重奏沒有指揮，所以比較簡單、比較自由。: A quartet has no conductor, so it is simpler and freer.
四重奏的座位也影響聲音。常見的排法是第一小提琴在左前、第二小提琴在右前，中提琴與: Seating affects the sound too. The usual arrangement puts the first violin front left and the second violin front right, with the viola and cello in the back row — which side each takes varies from group to group; the four sit in a shallow arc so that everyone can see the others' bows. This is not for looks but for seeing the attack: with no conductor, the four can only stay together through bow movement, breathing and eye contact. Sit too far apart or too scattered and the ensemble's reactions lag by half a beat.
四重奏的曲目形式也和這個編制綁在一起。最常見的結構是四個樂章：一個快板、一個慢板: The shape of the repertoire is tied to the line-up as well. The commonest structure is four movements: a fast one, a slow one, a dance-like one and a fast finale. This multi-movement plan lets the four switch between tempos and temperaments, and gives listeners time to compare one group's sound under different characters. The slow movement tests the second violin and the viola in particular: with the melody in the first violin or the cello, the inner parts have to hold the harmony at the smallest possible volume without disappearing.
弓法與音色也必須統一。四個人用同一種弓速、同一種壓力、同一種換弦方式，聲音才會融: Bowing and timbre have to be unified as well. Only when the four use the same bow speed, the same pressure and the same way of crossing strings does the sound blend. That unity does not come from a conductor's shout; it comes from copying each other in rehearsal — one player finds a good sound and the others reproduce it.
弦樂四重奏的場合從音樂廳的室內樂系列、私人沙龍、婚禮、錄音室，到大學與比賽。曲目: A string quartet turns up in concert-hall chamber series, private salons, weddings, recording studios, universities and competitions. The repertoire centres on the quartet literature that grew from the eighteenth century onwards, but also takes in arranged pop songs, film music and jazz. The line-up is small enough for a living room and big enough to carry a whole concert.
弦樂四重奏（String Quartet）— 兩把小提琴、中提琴、大提琴，四個平: String Quartet — two violins, viola and cello: four equal parts and no conductor. Ensembles and instrumentation by Next Door Sound Weavers.
弦樂四重奏（string quartet）是兩把小提琴、一把中提琴、一把大提琴的: A string quartet is a four-part line-up of two violins, a viola and a cello, with no conductor. It is not defined as four people playing strings, but as four equal parts that cover high, middle and low with the smallest possible line-up and stay together by hearing each other.
找現場演出。四重奏的細節在錄音裡容易被壓縮，現場才聽得出四個人怎麼互相聽。: Go and hear one live. A recording tends to squeeze a quartet's detail flat; only in the hall can you hear how the four listen to each other.
排練的內容也能說明這個編制的性格。四重奏的排練通常從「聽」開始，而不是從「演奏」: What happens in rehearsal says something about the character of the line-up too. A quartet's rehearsal usually begins with listening rather than playing: one player bows a phrase, then another plays the same phrase, the two are compared for timbre and intonation, and only then does everyone play together. This is slow, but it is the only way four people build a shared sound. With no conductor to give orders, every decision has to be heard, agreed and remembered by all four. A quartet's understanding therefore does not appear by itself with time; it accumulates through one concrete discussion after another.
最容易被混為一談的是弦樂團（string orchestra）。兩者同屬弦樂家族: The easiest confusion is with the string orchestra. Both belong to the string family, but a string orchestra usually adds double basses, has a conductor and can thicken its sections, whereas a quartet has no conductor and one player to a part. An orchestra can produce bigger dynamics and a thicker sound; in a quartet every player has to stand alone, and anyone's intonation or bowing will be heard.
根音、低音線、節奏核心；也常唱旋律: Roots, the bass line, the rhythmic core; often sings the melody as well
沒有指揮意味著沒有人可以怪。速度、音準、弓法都必須由四個人當場協商，排練的成本與: No conductor means there is nobody to blame. Tempo, intonation and bowing all have to be agreed between the four on the spot, so rehearsal costs and concentration go up rather than down.
為什麼是弦樂而不是別的樂器做這種四聲部編制？因為弦樂可以連續發聲、可以無限變化音: Why strings and not other instruments for this four-part line-up? Because strings can sound continuously, change volume without limit and adjust timbre instantly with bow speed and pressure, and because the four instruments share one timbre. Four different wind instruments can play four parts too, but their timbres differ so much that blending has to be calculated; four strings of one family already sound alike, so the question of balance returns to pure musical judgement. That is why the string quartet became the standard form for chamber writing: it lets a composer handle the most complex part-writing with the fewest timbral variables.
第二小提琴不是「拉得比較差的第一小提琴」。它的工作是讓第一小提琴聽起來好：同一條: The second violin is not a first violin played worse. Its job is to make the first violin sound good: on the same melody the second violin props from below in thirds or sixths and the first violin's outline becomes clear; prop too thickly and it blurs, too thinly and it sounds hollow. This is a completely different technique — judging when not to be heard. Many of a quartet's hard problems lie not in the first violin but in whether the second violin and the viola are willing to press their sound down to exactly the right level.
第二小提琴是「比較弱的第一小提琴」，所以由程度較差的人拉。: The second violin is a weaker first violin, so it goes to the less able player.
第二小提琴是獨立聲部，負責和聲的內線與旋律的支撐。它的技術重點是什麼時候不出聲，: The second violin is an independent part, carrying the inner line of the harmony and the support under the melody. Its technique turns on when not to sound, which is nothing like the first violin's.
聽四個人換弓是否同步。沒有指揮，換弓的一致性就是合奏的溫度計。: Listen for whether the four change bow together. With no conductor, the unanimity of the bow changes is the ensemble's thermometer.
聽聲部交換。旋律從一把琴換到另一把琴時，音色會變，這就是四重奏的對話感。: Listen for the exchange of parts. When the melody passes from one instrument to another the timbre changes, and that is the quartet's sense of dialogue.
聽速度的彈性。注意樂句結尾四個人怎麼一起放慢、怎麼一起回到原速。: Listen for flexibility of tempo. Notice how the four slow down together at the end of a phrase and come back to tempo together.
與鋼琴三重奏（鋼琴、小提琴、大提琴）的差別在聲部數與平衡。三重奏的和聲由鋼琴一手: The difference from a piano trio (piano, violin, cello) is the number of parts and the balance. In a trio the piano supplies the harmony on its own and the strings are two lines; a quartet has no piano, so the harmony has to be shared out among four string parts, which puts more work on the inner voices.
通常唱旋律、決定樂句呼吸；在大多數曲子裡是速度的提議者: Usually plays the melody and decides where the phrase breathes; in most works the one who proposes the tempo
通常由第一小提琴提議樂句的方向：一個吸氣、一個弓的起動、一個身體的前傾，就是起拍: The first violin usually proposes the direction of the phrase: an intake of breath, the start of a bow, a lean of the body — that is the upbeat. But proposing is not commanding. If the cello's bass line needs more room, or the viola's harmony needs a little more time, the others pull the tempo back with bow speed, breathing or a glance. These adjustments are ground into consensus in rehearsal and are immediate in performance. The same quartet will therefore take different tempos on different nights — not because it is imprecise, but because it is alive.
還有一種四重奏特有的寫作手法：聲部交換。旋律會從第一小提琴交給第二小提琴，再交給: There is also a writing device particular to the quartet: the exchange of parts. The melody passes from the first violin to the second, then to the viola or the cello. This is not display; it brings each of the four timbres into the foreground in turn, making a conversation instead of melody plus accompaniment. And because there is no conductor, quartet rehearsals often run longer than the performances: every flexibility has to be discussed first before anyone dares to use it on stage.
音準也是互相靠攏的。四重奏沒有指揮給基準音，通常由大提琴或第一小提琴給一個音，其: Intonation also leans towards the others. A quartet has no conductor to give a reference pitch, so usually the cello or the first violin gives a note and the others tune to it. In actual playing, intonation is adjusted by harmonic position: major thirds pressed low, minor thirds opened wide, fifths tuned pure. Inside one chord the four have to shade in the same direction at the same moment, and what they go by is the beating — the closer two notes come to just intonation, the slower the beats, until they vanish.
默契有幫助，但四重奏是可以被訓練的：固定排練、固定弓法、固定聽的順序，比私交更決: Rapport helps, but a quartet can be trained: a fixed rehearsal, fixed bowings and a fixed order of listening decide the stability of the ensemble more than friendship does.
